newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice market quiet, exports seen below target.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice market quiet, exports seen below target.

text.p: Thai rice prices were steady to lower this week as the market remained in the doldrums amid an absence of major buying orders, trade sources said on Friday.
Somboon Pataichant, manager of the Thai Rice Exporters Association, told Reuters there were only small orders from regular customers such as Hong Kong and Singapore.
"Activities remained focused on covering contracts for deliveries. There were no major leads in the market," he said.
Relatively slow rice trading since January forced the Thai commerce ministry to revise the export target for this year down to 5.0 million tonnes from 5.5 million tonnes projected earlier.
The export during January 1-May 28 was estimated at 1.80 million tonnes, trailing far behind 2.36 million tonnes during the same period last year.
"We hope that demand for Thai rice will pick up in the second half of 1997 as the supplies of our competitors run out," Somboon said.

Traders said they expected fresh orders to emerge soon as prices continued to soften. "There are some inquiries but I guess buyers want to pressure the prices down further before entering the market again," said one trader from a major exporting company.
Thai benchmark 100 percent B grade was quoted around $332-360 per tonne FOB Bangkok versus $335-360 last week. The 100 percent fragrant rice was steady at $690-710 per tonne on the same basis.
